nlohmann/json — single-header amalgamation
version:  3.12.0
source:   https://github.com/nlohmann/json/releases/download/v3.12.0/json.hpp
sha256:   aaf127c04cb31c406e5b04a63f1ae89369fccde6d8fa7cdda1ed4f32dfc5de63
obtained: 2026-07-16
license:  MIT (see header block at top of json.hpp)

nlohmann/json_fwd.hpp — matching forward declarations
version:  3.12.0
source:   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nlohmann/json/v3.12.0/single_include/nlohmann/json_fwd.hpp
sha256:   fb6aa70cbece087f37ab4685c182b287c53be54f785f981b9db9d30d2d028b37
obtained: 2026-08-10
license:  MIT (see header block at top of json_fwd.hpp)

Note: Homebrew ships nlohmann-json 3.12.0 as the *split* multi-header
distribution (json.hpp #includes ~31 nlohmann/ sub-headers), which is not
self-contained. We vendor the official single-header amalgamation of the
same version so the worker build has no external include-path dependency on
Homebrew for JSON.

json_fwd.hpp is vendored for the SAME reason and was originally missed. Six
benchmark headers (`worker/src/benchmark/{CaseParser,DeepAudit,Execution,
Artifacts,SelectorParser,SemanticValidation}.h`) include <nlohmann/json_fwd.hpp>
for forward declarations only. With no vendored copy that resolved to whatever
the system happened to install, and nothing declares the dependency — there is
no find_package(nlohmann_json) anywhere in the build. macOS stayed green purely
because Homebrew also ships 3.12.0. On Debian 13 (nlohmann-json3-dev 3.11.3) the
two headers put DIFFERENT inline ABI namespaces into namespace nlohmann, and
every reference to json_pointer becomes ambiguous. Keep both files at the same
version; the ABI-tag guard at the top of each only fires when both are vendored.
